clue.text: Men entitled to see one in London hospital

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece sits inside the hospital's name

parts.note: Barts is the familiar name of St Bartholomew's Hospital in London
taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to visit someone in a London hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: BARTS is St Bartholomew's, a famous London hospital; put ONE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Baronets hold a hereditary title, so they are literally men with a title to their names.

clue.text: Herb uses silver-lined drill

indicators.note: lined means the metal forms a lining inside the drill word

parts.note: to bore is to drill
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A herb uses a silver-lined drill.
explanation.definitionFit: Borage is a blue-flowered plant used in salads and drinks.

clue.text: More ruddy toing and froing!

indicators.note: going to and fro means the word reads the same either way

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An exclamation about rosy cheeks from rushing back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome: 'toing and froing' says it reads the same forwards and backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruddy means red-faced, so more ruddy is comparatively redder in tone.

clue.text: Refusal to turn informer, however inquisitive

parts.note: no is a refusal
to sing is slang for confessing to police

explanation.surface: Refusing to grass on others, however curious they are.
explanation.walkthrough: SING is criminal slang for informing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosing means prying, poking one's nose into things.

clue.text: At that point, repeatedly offered words of comfort

indicators.note: repeatedly means the word is given twice

parts.note: there means at that place or point

explanation.surface: Soothing phrases offered again and again at a certain moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing phrase said to calm a crying child.

clue.text: Tom's at university? What a sauce!

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, so Tom's gives cat's
up means in residence at university in British usage

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at the cheek of a man called Tom being at university.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom looks like a name; it is a male cat. Being UP is being at university in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Catsup is an old variant of ketchup, a tomato condiment.

clue.text: Capsules needed for American hens

parts.note: poules is French for hens

explanation.surface: Containers required to house American chickens.
explanation.walkthrough: POULES is the French word for hens.
explanation.definitionFit: Ampoules are small sealed glass vials of medicine.

clue.text: No local involved Rex in road rage

indicators.note: in places the king's letter inside the road and rage pieces

parts.note: St is street, a road
anger is rage
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An outsider was involved in a road-rage incident with a man called Rex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' is a link; 'in' places R between ST and ANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from elsewhere is an outsider, not a resident.

clue.text: Still room to retain education of a formal nature

indicators.note: to retain means to hold the education letters within

parts.note: a stillroom in a British country house was a storeroom, a pantry

explanation.surface: A quiet room keeping formal schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: A stillroom is a British country-house storeroom, here a pantry; 'Still' is not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantry is excessive concern with correct rules and form.

clue.text: Soldiers get meals containing vegetable

definitions.note: the singular stands for the plural crop

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of soldiers
dishes are courses or meals

explanation.surface: Troops are given food with some greens in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Radishes are crunchy red root crops eaten in salads.

clue.text: Pole cut down and saved

parts.note: S stands for the South Pole
pared means trimmed or reduced

explanation.surface: A post was chopped down and then rescued.
explanation.walkthrough: Pole looks like a post to cut; it is S for South.
explanation.definitionFit: Spared means kept from harm, rescued.

clue.text: Unruly teenager takes to drink

indicators.note: an unruly thing is out of order, so the letters of teenager are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebellious adolescent starts drinking heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes to drink' suggests alcohol; the drink is a mild tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Green tea is an unfermented tea brewed as a beverage.

clue.text: Inform against knight in Italian city

indicators.note: in places the chess piece inside the city name

parts.note: Turin is a city in northern Italy
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Someone betrays a knight living in an Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn someone in is to report them to the police.

clue.text: The college day started

parts.note: an institute is a college

explanation.surface: The college term began on a particular day.
explanation.definitionFit: Instituted means set up or initiated.

clue.text: What drivers often do to make redress

explanation.surface: Motorists frequently fix their mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read redress as re-dress: gear is clothing, so changing one's gear is putting on new clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorists shift the gearbox into another ratio; a person putting on fresh clothing swaps outfits.

clue.text: Partied in old, second-hand motor initially

indicators.note: initially places the vehicle word first in the order

parts.note: a motor is a car
used means second-hand

explanation.surface: Someone had a party in an old used car.
explanation.definitionFit: To carouse is to drink and make merry noisily.

clue.text: Will pearl and sue go haywire?

indicators.note: to go haywire is to go wild, so the letters of pearl and sue are mixed up

explanation.surface: A question whether two people named Pearl and Sue will run amok.
explanation.walkthrough: Will looks like the future verb; it is the noun for wish, as in 'at Her Majesty's pleasure'.
explanation.definitionFit: Will and pleasure both mean desire or wish.

clue.text: Godless men commit robbery in a back street

indicators.note: in places the crime word inside the street phrase
back means the street abbreviation is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: a heist is a robbery

explanation.surface: Unbelievers carry out a robbery in a back street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ST into TS; HEIST goes inside A + TS. 'commit' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheists are people who deny that any deity exists.

clue.text: Everyone has to repeat using the same initial sound

definitions.note: the phrase describes the verb's action

parts.note: all means everyone
iterate means to say or do again

explanation.surface: Everybody must repeat words that start alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To alliterate is to begin neighbouring words with the same consonant, as in a tongue-twister.

clue.text: Obstruction by Henry proves fatal

parts.note: a let is an obstruction, as in without let or hindrance
Hal is a nickname for Henry

explanation.surface: A blockade by a man called Henry turns deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: LET means hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethal means deadly.

clue.text: Obvious way to protect one's invention

explanation.surface: A clear way to safeguard an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means plain or evident; as a noun it is the legal right protecting an inventor.

clue.text: Facts the German needed on sexual orientation

parts.note: gen is slang for information or facts
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: German information required about sexuality.
explanation.definitionFit: Gender concerns male or female identity, loosely meant here by the setter's phrase.

clue.text: Ass and old horse acquired with some reluctance

parts.note: a nag is a horse, usually a poor one
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone grudgingly bought a donkey and an aged horse.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, the hesitant noise, conveys reluctance.
explanation.definitionFit: The onager is a wild donkey of Asia.

clue.text: Hardly the accommodation for posh passengers!

definitions.text: Hardly the accommodation for posh passengers!

parts.words: Hardly the accommodation for posh passengers!
parts.note: the cheapest section of an old passenger ship, far from the first-class cabins

explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the lowest-fare part of a ship, used by poorer emigrants.

clue.text: Vegetable and fruit drink

explanation.surface: A shopping list of produce and juice.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a squash is a fruit cordial diluted with water.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourd such as butternut is one sense; a concentrated cordial diluted with water is the British soft-drink sense.

clue.text: Ambassador enters to listen finally

indicators.note: enters means the envoy's letters go into the verb for hearing

parts.note: to attend is to listen or pay heed
HE is His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: An envoy comes in to hear the conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: HE, His Excellency, is the form of address for an ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: At the end means at last, eventually.

clue.text: Residing in a good address, you must look smart

indicators.note: the letters live inside the words address you

explanation.surface: Advice that a posh home calls for stylish appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressy describes elegant, formal clothing.

clue.text: One leotard designed for a figure worshipper

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: designed means made into a new shape, so leotard is rearranged

explanation.surface: A single leotard made for someone who idolises a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships images or statues as gods.
